lessons.title: Meet Xolos
lessons.subtitle: A club from the border

story.title: A name to remember
story.body: Club Tijuana is also known as Xolos. Its longer name, Xoloitzcuintles, gives the club a distinctive identity. Start by connecting the short name to the club rather than memorizing every letter at once. The club represents Tijuana, a city in Baja California. That geographical connection is the first anchor for this roadmap.

story.title: The home ground
story.body: Estadio Caliente is the home ground to associate with Xolos. Keep three pieces together: Club Tijuana, the city of Tijuana, and Estadio Caliente. They answer different questions—who, where, and which venue. In the activities that follow, practice those connections in both directions. You do not need a current squad list to recognize the club and begin understanding its story.

lessons.title: The climb
lessons.subtitle: From a new club to champions

story.title: Three years to anchor
story.body: The Xolos story starts in 2007. The next major anchor is promotion to Mexico’s top division in 2011. Those dates describe different milestones: beginning a club and earning a place in a higher division. Keeping the events separate is more useful than learning an isolated list of numbers.

story.title: A rapid rise
story.body: The third anchor is Apertura 2012, when Xolos won their first top-flight league championship. Follow the sequence: founded in 2007, promoted in 2011, champions in 2012. When recalling the years, say the event alongside the number. The next lesson explores the final behind that title. This is a historical sequence, not a statement about the club’s current standings.

lessons.title: The 2012 final
lessons.subtitle: The night a title became history

story.title: The opponent
story.body: Xolos faced Toluca in the Apertura 2012 final. A final is easier to remember as a story with two sides than as a title in a trophy list. The opponent matters because it lets you connect the achievement to an actual contest. For this lesson, the relevant championship is the 2012 Apertura, not an undated league title.

story.title: The result
story.body: Xolos won the two-leg final 4–1 on aggregate and secured the championship on December 2, 2012. Aggregate means the goals across both legs are combined; it is not the score of a single match. Practice the opponent, the aggregate result, and the title date as separate facts. Together they provide a compact account of a defining moment in the club’s history.

lessons.title: Duvier Riascos
lessons.subtitle: A forward’s route to Tijuana

story.title: Meet the player
story.body: Duvier Riascos is a Colombian forward. Learn the country and position as separate connections: where the player comes from and the role he plays. This lesson focuses on the period around his move to Xolos, rather than presenting an up-to-date career profile. Historical scope helps you avoid confusing a former club with a current one.

story.title: The previous stop
story.body: Before joining Xolos for Clausura 2012, Riascos played for Puebla in Apertura 2011. That sequence gives you a small piece of his career path: Puebla, then Club Tijuana. Recall the club name with the period attached. The questions here are about that move, his Colombian origin, and his forward role. They do not ask which team he represents today.

lessons.title: Fernando Arce
lessons.subtitle: A midfielder with a local connection

story.title: A local connection
story.body: Fernando Arce is described by the club as a midfielder from Tijuana. Those two details make useful anchors: the role he played and his local connection. A player’s birthplace or hometown is different from his club affiliation. Separating those relationships helps you understand a profile instead of remembering a single label.

story.title: Place him in the story
story.body: During Apertura 2012, Arce represented Xolos. The club’s interview from that tournament connects his name to the team and its preparations. For now, learn three concise relationships: Arce to midfield, Arce to Tijuana, and Arce to Xolos during Apertura 2012. Later content can expand his career without replacing these historically scoped foundations. This lesson does not describe his current role or employer.

lessons.title: Cirilo Saucedo
lessons.subtitle: Reading a goalkeeper’s numbers

story.title: Between the posts
story.body: Cirilo Saucedo played as a goalkeeper for Xolos. Goalkeeper statistics need precise context: goals conceded in a regular phase are different from goals conceded across a whole tournament with playoffs. This lesson uses the Clausura 2012 regular phase, as reported in the club’s announcement about award nominations.

story.title: Keep the scope attached
story.body: Saucedo conceded 11 goals in 17 regular-phase matches during Clausura 2012. Learn the pair together—11 goals, 17 matches—then attach the tournament and phase. These are historical numbers, not a live performance total. When comparing players later, check that their numbers cover the same type of period. The exercises here ask about Saucedo’s role and these two specifically scoped figures.

lessons.title: Meet Madrid
lessons.subtitle: A name, a city, a beginning

story.title: The club and the city
story.body: Real Madrid is the club at the center of this roadmap. Connect its name to Madrid before adding players, titles, and matches. A club’s identity is a useful starting point because many later facts will refer back to it. Keep club and city as distinct ideas, even when the city is part of the name.

story.title: The starting year
story.body: The club traces its beginning to 1902, when the first board of Madrid Foot Ball Club was elected on March 6. For this introductory lesson, remember the founding year rather than trying to learn every administrative detail. Your three anchors are the club name, Madrid, and 1902. The next lesson follows the story into the early European Cup era.

lessons.title: European roots
lessons.subtitle: The first five European Cups

story.title: A European beginning
story.body: Real Madrid won the first European Cup in 1956. The competition name matters: this is the historical European Cup era, before the modern Champions League name. Use 1956 as the starting anchor, then connect it to the run that followed rather than treating each trophy as an unrelated fact.

story.title: The early run
story.body: Madrid won the first five European Cups consecutively, from 1956 through 1960. Alfredo Di Stéfano is one of the players the club associates with that era. These three anchors—1956, five consecutive titles, and Di Stéfano—help you recognize the period. They describe an early chapter of the club’s history, not its current total of European trophies or a ranking of every player.

lessons.title: La Décima
lessons.subtitle: An equalizer that changed a final

story.title: The setting
story.body: In 2014, Real Madrid faced Atlético in the Champions League final. The match became the night of La Décima, Madrid’s tenth European Cup. Learn the year and opponent before the decisive event. That context lets you connect the story to the correct final rather than mixing it with another Madrid title.

story.title: The turning point
story.body: Sergio Ramos scored the equalizer in added time, sending the final into extra time. Madrid then won the match. For this lesson, focus on the turning point: Ramos’s goal changed what could have been a defeat into another period of play. Recall the opponent, the year, and the equalizer’s scorer. The player lessons connect those facts to individual careers.

lessons.title: Cristiano Ronaldo
lessons.subtitle: A forward in the 2014 story

story.title: Meet the forward
story.body: Cristiano Ronaldo is a forward associated with Real Madrid’s history. This card focuses on that part of his career, not his current club. Learn his name and role before adding a long list of statistics. Club associations need a time frame, especially for players whose careers include several teams.

story.title: A final connection
story.body: Ronaldo scored a penalty for Real Madrid in the 2014 Champions League final. That connects his player card to the La Décima lesson. The three facts here are his forward role, his Real Madrid career association, and the penalty in that final. You can use the same event to understand a player and a club without counting it as two independent memories.

lessons.title: Sergio Ramos
lessons.subtitle: A defender with a scoring story

story.title: The defender
story.body: Sergio Ramos played as a defender for Real Madrid. His equalizer in the 2014 Champions League final is a key event to connect to that role. A position tells you a player’s usual responsibilities; it does not limit the kinds of decisive contributions he can make in a match.

story.title: A scoped total
story.body: Real Madrid’s historical player profile records 101 goals for Ramos during his club career. Keep the club scope attached: this is not a total for every team he represented. Your three anchors are defender, scorer of the 2014 equalizer, and 101 Real Madrid goals. The equalizer also appears in the club lesson, so review should recognize it as shared knowledge rather than demand duplicate work.

lessons.title: Iker Casillas
lessons.subtitle: The goalkeeper’s long chapter

story.title: Meet the goalkeeper
story.body: Iker Casillas is a goalkeeper in Real Madrid’s historical player collection. His first-team debut came in 1999. Connect the player to his position and then to the beginning of his senior Madrid career. This is a historical profile, so the lesson does not ask which club he plays for today.

story.title: An appearance total
story.body: The club records 725 official Real Madrid appearances for Casillas. “Official” and “Real Madrid” both belong with that number: it is not a total of every appearance for club and country. Practice goalkeeper, 1999, and 725 as three distinct facts. Together they provide a compact introduction to his long first-team chapter and a foundation for later lessons about his matches and achievements.

lessons.title: AEK Athens in Europe

story.body: UEFA records Semi-finals (2005/06, 2021/22) as Villarreal’s best European Cup performance, giving this season’s campaign a longer story to follow.

lessons.title: SV Werder Bremen club guide
lessons.subtitle: A short, source-backed introduction to the club.

story.title: A club with history
story.body: SV Werder Bremen is included in the official 2026/27 Bundesliga club overview. Werder won the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double in 2003/04.

story.title: Home and heritage
story.body: The Bundesliga profile lists Weserstadion as SV Werder Bremen’s ground; the club’s history also includes this milestone: 2003/04.

lessons.title: Iker Casillas: A captain’s honours
lessons.subtitle: Club success and Spain’s golden era

story.title: A long Madrid chapter
story.body: Casillas’s Real Madrid career brought him 19 titles as a madridista. Three were Champions League trophies, part of an honours collection built over many seasons. Those honours add a new layer to his 725 official appearances: the goalkeeper was central to teams that repeatedly reached the top of Europe.

story.title: A champion with Spain
story.body: His international story reached its high point with Spain’s 2010 World Cup win. He also lifted the European Championship in 2008 and again in 2012. Keep the two chapters distinct: Madrid’s 19 titles belong to his club career, while the World Cup and two Euros came with Spain.

lessons.title: Sergio Ramos: A defender’s trophy haul
lessons.subtitle: Four European Cups among 22 titles

story.title: A decorated Madrid career
story.body: Across 16 seasons with Real Madrid, Sergio Ramos collected 22 titles. The defender’s haul included four European Cups, a remarkable return for a player whose decisive moments became part of the club’s biggest nights. His record extends well beyond the 2014 equalizer already connected to La Décima.

story.title: Different competitions, one legacy
story.body: Ramos’s honours also included five LaLiga titles. He captained Madrid through European success and lifted the trophies as the team moved into a new era. Remember the scale of the collection by keeping its parts separate: 22 titles overall, four European Cups, and five Spanish league championships.

lessons.title: Xolos: The road to the top flight
lessons.subtitle: Early milestones on the climb

story.title: A professional beginning
story.body: Club Tijuana’s professional story began with a match on January 14, 2007. Its first title followed in the Apertura 2010 Liga de Ascenso, the second-tier competition. Winning that tournament was a milestone in its own right, but it did not yet mean promotion: Xolos still had to win a separate two-leg promotion final.

story.title: The climb becomes real
story.body: After the promotion final against Irapuato, Xolos reached Mexico’s top flight in 2011. The club’s Primera División history began on July 23, 2011, against Morelia, with Joe Corona scoring its first goal in that division. Keep the first professional match, the second-tier title, and the top-flight debut as three different milestones.

lessons.title: Madrid’s modern European run
lessons.subtitle: From a three-peat to the 15th crown

story.title: Three in a row
story.body: Madrid’s 2018 victory in Kyiv completed a third consecutive Champions League triumph and brought its European Cup total to 13. That three-peat closed a remarkable five-season stretch in which the club won the competition four times. It connects the earlier European story to a modern period of sustained success.

story.title: The count keeps climbing
story.body: The European Cup count reached 14 when Madrid beat Liverpool in the 2022 final in Paris. Two years later, a win over Borussia Dortmund at Wembley brought the club to 15. Follow the sequence by attaching each number to its year: 13 in 2018, 14 in 2022, and 15 in 2024.

lessons.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Madrid’s scoring legacy
lessons.subtitle: A remarkable scoring rate and a European trophy haul

story.title: More than a goal per game
story.body: Cristiano Ronaldo played for Real Madrid from 2009 to 2018. The club’s official profile records 451 goals in 438 official matches, a scoring rate above one per game. Across competitions, 105 of those Madrid goals came in the Champions League.

story.title: A champion in Europe
story.body: His Madrid years also brought four Champions League titles. The profile presents those trophies alongside his club scoring records: 451 goals overall, including 105 in Europe’s leading club competition. His Madrid chapter combined individual output with repeated team success.

lessons.title: Fernando Arce: From Irapuato to Tijuana
lessons.subtitle: A long Mexican career brought him back to his hometown club

story.title: A first-division beginning
story.body: Fernando Arce took his early youth steps at América, then made his Mexican first-division debut with Irapuato on 28 October 2000. After three seasons, he moved to Veracruz in the Verano 2002 tournament, where he became a regular starter.

story.title: International and club milestones
story.body: Arce made his senior Mexico debut on 4 February 2003 and later played at the 2007 Gold Cup and Copa América. He joined Santos Laguna for Clausura 2008 and helped the club reach the final with a key semifinal goal against Monterrey. Later, his hometown team Club Tijuana signed him from Santos.

lessons.title: Duvier Riascos: Goals across continents
lessons.subtitle: A Colombian forward built a career in South America, China, and Mexico

story.title: A career starts in Colombia
story.body: Duvier Riascos began his professional career with América de Cali in 2005. His path later crossed into China, where he won the 2010 Chinese Super League scoring title while representing Shanghai Shenhua. The club’s signing profile celebrates the scoring crown as one of his standout individual achievements.

story.title: A chapter in Tijuana
story.body: After playing for Puebla in Apertura 2011, Riascos joined Club Tijuana for Clausura 2012. A 2019 Xolos retrospective recalls him as one of the club’s title-era figures and credits him with 23 goals in 65 matches for the team. It describes a career that continued after his Tijuana spell, including a move to Universidad Católica in 2019.

lessons.title: Cirilo Saucedo: Club and country
lessons.subtitle: A youth medal, a senior debut, and the move to Xolos

story.title: A medal with Mexico’s under-23s
story.body: Before his long top-flight career, Cirilo Saucedo also represented Mexico at youth level. Club Tijuana’s profile notes that he was part of the Mexico under-23 squad that won bronze at the 2003 Pan American Games in Santo Domingo.

story.title: From Tigres to a Mexico debut
story.body: Club Tijuana announced Saucedo’s arrival from Tigres UANL ahead of Apertura 2011, its first top-flight tournament. In January 2013 he made his senior Mexico debut in a friendly against Denmark. These are two distinct career steps: a club move in 2011 and a senior international debut in 2013.

lessons.title: The European Cup begins
lessons.subtitle: An invitational tournament becomes a continental stage

story.title: A new European contest
story.body: The competition now known as the UEFA Champions League began in the 1955/56 season. Its original name was the European Champion Clubs’ Cup, a direct description of its aim: bring leading club sides from different countries into one European contest.

story.title: A small field, a lasting idea
story.body: That first edition was an invitational tournament with 16 teams. Clubs were invited to take part, so the opening field was not yet the modern qualifying path from national leagues. The competition’s name and entry system would change, but the idea of a European club champion started here.

lessons.title: From groups to one league phase
lessons.subtitle: The Champions League changes shape

story.title: A new name and a new stage
story.body: The European Cup introduced its first group stage in 1991/92. The Champions League name followed in 1992/93. These are separate milestones: a change in the tournament structure, followed by the identity associated with its next era.

story.title: A shared table
story.body: Beginning in 2024/25, the group stage gave way to a league phase with 36 clubs. Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents: four at home and four away. Unlike a traditional round-robin league, clubs do not face every other participant.

lessons.title: Istanbul: a final turned around
lessons.subtitle: Liverpool’s 2005 comeback against Milan

story.title: A steep half-time deficit
story.body: At half-time of the 2005 final in Istanbul, AC Milan led Liverpool 3–0. Liverpool answered with three goals in seven minutes, leveling the match at 3–3 and carrying it into extra time.

story.title: A champion decided by penalties
story.body: Neither team scored in extra time, so the final went to a penalty shoot-out. Liverpool won the shoot-out 3–2 and lifted the trophy after one of the competition’s most memorable comebacks. Keep the match score separate from the shoot-out score: 3–3, then Liverpool 3–2 on penalties.

lessons.title: A national league takes shape
lessons.subtitle: The Bundesliga begins in the 1960s

story.title: A single top division
story.body: On July 28, 1962, the German Football Association voted to introduce a national single-division top flight. The plan brought a new national competition together from the regional structure that had preceded it.

story.title: The first season
story.body: The Bundesliga began in 1963/64 with 16 clubs. That inaugural season established the league as Germany’s national top division. The start date, its nationwide structure, and its opening field size explain what made the new competition different.

lessons.title: A league grows, then settles
lessons.subtitle: How reunification changed the field

story.title: The first expansion
story.body: The Bundesliga expanded from 16 to 18 clubs in 1965/66. The 18-club setup became the familiar shape of the competition, though one historic season would briefly make the league larger.

story.title: One season of 20 clubs
story.body: After German reunification, the 1991/92 Bundesliga admitted 20 clubs, including the East German sides Hansa Rostock and Dynamo Dresden. The league returned to 18 teams the following season, 1992/93. That temporary change tied league size to a major national turning point.

lessons.title: Leverkusen’s unbeaten season
lessons.subtitle: The 2023/24 champions finish without a loss

story.title: A first for the league
story.body: Bayer Leverkusen clinched their first Bundesliga title on Matchday 29 of the 2023/24 season. They kept winning and drawing after securing the championship, then completed all 34 league matches without a defeat.

story.title: An unbeaten campaign
story.body: Leverkusen finished the 2023/24 Bundesliga with 28 wins, six draws, and zero losses. It was the first time a team completed a full Bundesliga season unbeaten. The feat belongs to that completed season, not to an ongoing record that could change.

lessons.title: The roots of Mexico’s top flight
lessons.subtitle: A professional league, then a new identity

story.title: The professional roots
story.body: Mexico’s professional First Division began in 1943/44. This is the historical starting point of the top flight. Its Spanish name, Primera División, describes its place at the top of the domestic league structure.

story.title: The Liga MX identity
story.body: The Liga MX project was presented in 2012. That modern identity came decades after the first professional season. Keep the two dates separate: 1943/44 for the professional roots, and 2012 for the Liga MX launch.

lessons.title: Two title races
lessons.subtitle: From Invierno and Verano to Apertura and Clausura

story.title: A split calendar
story.body: Mexico’s short-tournament era began with Invierno 1996. The structure created two title races within a football season. The first labels were Invierno and Verano: winter and summer.

story.title: Read the tournament label
story.body: Later editions use Apertura and Clausura. A championship belongs to its named tournament, so a year alone is not enough to identify the title. Some editions have special names, including Bicentenario and Guard1anes. Read the full label before comparing winners.

lessons.title: Santos and the short-tournament era
lessons.subtitle: A first crown and the people behind it

story.title: A new era’s first winner
story.body: Santos Laguna won Invierno 1996, the first title in the short-tournament era and the club’s first league championship. Jared Borgetti arrived for that tournament and scored 16 goals in the title-winning campaign.

story.title: A champion returns as coach
story.body: Benjamín Galindo was a player in that first Santos championship. He later returned as the coach who won Clausura 2012. The two milestones connect a person to one club across different roles and generations.

lessons.title: A new English league
lessons.subtitle: The 1992 launch and its first champions

story.title: A new competition
story.body: The Premier League was established in 1992. Its first campaign, 1992/93, began with 22 clubs; the later 20-club format should not be applied to that opening season.

story.title: The first champions
story.body: Manchester United won the inaugural Premier League title. This starts a new competition’s history, rather than the whole history of English top-flight football.

lessons.title: An unbeaten league season
lessons.subtitle: Arsenal’s 2003/04 league record

story.title: The Invincibles
story.body: Arsenal completed the 2003/04 Premier League campaign without losing a league match. The claim applies to that league season, not every competition Arsenal played in.

story.title: Wins and draws
story.body: Their 38 league games consisted of 26 wins and 12 draws. Those two totals tell the story of an unbeaten campaign; they are separate from Arsenal’s longer unbeaten run across seasons.

lessons.title: Two Hall of Fame goalscorers
lessons.subtitle: Completed careers, league goals and scoring awards

story.title: Shearer’s league goals
story.body: The league’s 2021 Hall of Fame announcement credited Alan Shearer with 260 Premier League goals across Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United. That is a Premier League total, not a single-club or all-competitions total.

story.title: Henry’s Arsenal seasons
story.body: Thierry Henry scored 30 Premier League goals in Arsenal’s unbeaten 2003/04 season. The league’s 2021 Hall of Fame announcement also credited him with four Premier League Golden Boots across his career. A single-season goal total and a career award count describe different achievements.

lessons.title: Raúl · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Raúl’s story begins in Madrid. The club’s biography describes a forward whose development included its youth teams before his first-team debut in 1994.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: Keep youth arrival and senior debut separate: 1992 starts the profile’s broader club timeline, while 29 October 1994 is the first-team milestone.

lessons.title: Raúl · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Raúl finished his Madrid senior career with 741 appearances and 323 goals. Those figures belong to his club record, not to Spain or his later clubs.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: His three European titles connect that long career to the finals of 1998, 2000 and 2002. Learn the appearances, goals and title count as separate memories.

lessons.title: Karim Benzema · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Benzema was born in Lyon and arrived at Madrid in 2009. His club career continued through 2023, creating a long historical period to attach to his numbers.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: The 2022 Ballon d’Or is an individual award within that period. Keep the player’s birthplace, Madrid arrival and award year as three distinct anchors.

lessons.title: Karim Benzema · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Across his Madrid career, Benzema made 648 appearances and scored 354 goals. The club biography lists 25 team titles for that completed spell.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: A title count and a goal count measure different achievements. These questions use Madrid totals and do not combine his records at Lyon, later clubs or France.

lessons.title: Zinedine Zidane · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Zidane moved from Juventus to Madrid in 2001. A year later, his volley against Bayer Leverkusen became a defining moment of the European final.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: This path follows Zidane as a player. His later coaching career has its own dates and should not be added to his playing appearances.

lessons.title: Zinedine Zidane · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Zidane’s Madrid playing spell ended in 2006 with 227 appearances and 49 goals, according to the club biography.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: Remember the club and role alongside the totals: Madrid player, 2001–2006. These are not France caps, whole-career totals or matches managed.

lessons.title: Gareth Bale · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Bale arrived at Madrid in 2013 and made his debut against Villarreal that September. Later, his overhead kick against Liverpool became part of the club’s European final history.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: Keep the two opponents separate: Villarreal belongs to his Madrid debut, Liverpool to the 2018 final. The dates give each connection its own place.

lessons.title: Gareth Bale · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: The Madrid biography lists 258 appearances, 106 goals and five European title honours for Bale. These totals refer to his Madrid career.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: A trophy honour does not by itself say a player took the field in every final. Learn the club’s published honours count separately from individual match participation.

lessons.title: Roberto Carlos · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Roberto Carlos arrived from Inter in 1996. Madrid’s biography identifies him as a left back, giving his club move and playing role a clear historical context.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: Connect Inter to the previous stop and Madrid to the spell that began in 1996. This is a past transfer, not a current-club question.

lessons.title: Roberto Carlos · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Roberto Carlos left Madrid in 2007 after 527 appearances and 68 goals. Those figures describe his completed Madrid playing record.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: The departure date is not a retirement date. Keep the club spell separate from his earlier teams, later teams and appearances for Brazil.

lessons.title: Alfredo Di Stéfano · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Di Stéfano was born in Buenos Aires and played for Madrid from 1953 to 1964. Birthplace and club playing period are separate facts.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: He also later worked as a coach. These lessons keep his playing record separate from those later roles and from national-team appearances.

lessons.title: Alfredo Di Stéfano · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Madrid’s biography records 396 official appearances and 308 goals for Di Stéfano. His later Super Ballon d’Or was awarded in 1989.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: The award year lies outside his Madrid playing period. Use that separation to distinguish a career honour from a goal or appearance during a club spell.

lessons.title: Steven Gerrard · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Gerrard’s first Liverpool appearance came in 1998. He became captain in 2003 and lifted the European Cup in Istanbul in 2005.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: The three years describe different milestones: debut, captaincy and a title. Recall the event alongside its date instead of treating the years as an interchangeable list.

lessons.title: Steven Gerrard · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Gerrard made 710 Liverpool appearances and scored 186 Liverpool goals. His completed England career is a separate record of 114 caps.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: Club appearances and national-team caps use different scopes. In these questions, the named team tells you which total to retrieve.

lessons.title: Ian Rush · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Ian Rush had two Liverpool spells: 1980–1987 and 1988–1996. His year at Juventus sits between them rather than inside an uninterrupted Liverpool career.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: Follow the route as a sequence: first arrival, Juventus, Liverpool return. That structure helps explain why the club biography lists two separate playing periods.

lessons.title: Ian Rush · club record
lessons.subtitle: A completed playing career, with the scope kept clear

story.title: Place the story
story.body: Across both Liverpool spells, Rush recorded 660 appearances and 346 goals. The club’s account also gives 47 goals for his 1983/84 season.

story.title: Keep the scope
story.body: The season total is smaller because it covers one campaign. Match the scope to the number: both Liverpool spells for the career totals, 1983/84 for the season tally.

lessons.title: Messi’s Barcelona journey
lessons.subtitle: From Rosario to a long senior career at Barça

story.title: From Rosario
story.body: Lionel Messi was born in Rosario, Argentina. FC Barcelona’s player profile records his senior Barcelona years as 2004 to 2021, a span that began when he entered the first team as a teenager.

story.title: A career across generations
story.body: Messi’s first-team career at Barcelona began in 2004 and concluded in 2021. He remained with the club across many seasons, becoming a defining figure of the team’s modern era. Those dates describe his Barcelona senior span, rather than his full playing career elsewhere.

lessons.title: Messi’s Barcelona record
lessons.subtitle: Official appearances, goals and European honours

story.title: The club’s official count
story.body: FC Barcelona’s record article separates official first-team appearances from other matches. As of 27 May 2021, it credited Messi with 778 official appearances and 672 goals. The date matters: these are historical club totals reported at the close of his Barcelona chapter.

story.title: Success in Europe
story.body: Messi also won four European Cups with Barcelona. Together, the club-reported totals of 778 official appearances, 672 goals and four European Cups sketch his Barcelona record. They do not include later matches played after his departure.

lessons.title: Xavi’s Barcelona beginnings
lessons.subtitle: A Terrassa-born midfielder’s first-team journey

story.title: A local beginning
story.body: Xavi Hernández was born in Terrassa, Spain. Barcelona’s legend profile marks his senior debut in 1998, beginning a long first-team career with the club.

story.title: The end of his Barça playing chapter
story.body: Xavi’s final Barcelona season ended in 2015. After that season he continued his playing career elsewhere, so the 1998 debut and 2015 final season mark only his Barça first-team period.

lessons.title: Xavi’s Barcelona honours and games
lessons.subtitle: A long record of matches and major trophies

story.title: A Barça mainstay
story.body: Barcelona’s official legend profile records 767 games for Xavi. Across his Barcelona career, he won eight league titles, anchoring a period of sustained domestic success.

story.title: European champion
story.body: Xavi also lifted the Champions League four times with Barcelona. The club’s profile groups that European record with his 767 games and eight league titles; all three totals refer to his Barça career.

lessons.title: Lahm’s route back to Bayern
lessons.subtitle: A Stuttgart loan and leadership on two world stages

story.title: A loan spell away
story.body: Philipp Lahm spent a loan spell at VfB Stuttgart before returning to Bayern Munich. The Bayern Hall of Fame includes that detour in its account of his career, while his Bayern statistics count only his appearances for the Munich club.

story.title: Captain for club and country
story.body: Lahm captained Bayern to the 2013 Champions League title. A year later, he captained Germany to the 2014 World Cup. Those milestones belong to different teams: one was a Bayern club triumph, and the other an international title with Germany.

lessons.title: Lahm’s Bayern honours and appearances
lessons.subtitle: Competitive match totals and domestic cup success

story.title: A Bayern career counted in matches
story.body: Bayern’s Hall of Fame credits Philipp Lahm with 517 competitive appearances for the club. The total is scoped to Bayern and excludes his loan matches with VfB Stuttgart.

story.title: League and cup titles
story.body: Lahm won eight Bundesliga titles and six DFB Cups with Bayern. These domestic honours sit alongside the club’s 2013 European triumph, giving a picture of his success across league, cup and continental competition.

lessons.title: Schweinsteiger’s changing role
lessons.subtitle: From the wing into Bayern’s central midfield

story.title: A new position
story.body: Bastian Schweinsteiger began his Bayern career in a wide role. Under coach Louis van Gaal, he moved into central midfield, where he became an important organiser for the team.

story.title: A treble and a World Cup
story.body: In 2013 Schweinsteiger was part of Bayern’s treble-winning side. The following year he was part of Germany’s World Cup-winning team. One achievement came with Bayern, the other with his national team.

lessons.title: Schweinsteiger’s Bayern record
lessons.subtitle: Five hundred competitive matches and eight league titles

story.title: A long Bayern career
story.body: Bayern’s Hall of Fame records 500 competitive appearances and 68 goals for Schweinsteiger. Both numbers refer to his Bayern club career, rather than his appearances or goals for Germany.

story.title: Domestic success
story.body: Schweinsteiger won eight Bundesliga titles with Bayern. That domestic total belongs to his club honours; it is separate from the 2013 treble and his later international World Cup success with Germany.

lessons.title: Thierry Henry · career connections
lessons.subtitle: A move from Italy, a return to Arsenal and a national-team triumph

story.title: A new role in north London
story.body: Arsenal brought Henry from Juventus in 1999. He had played mainly as a winger in Italy; Arsène Wenger reshaped him into a striker, and his Arsenal career took off.

story.title: A return and an international memory
story.body: After leaving for Barcelona, Henry returned to Arsenal on loan in 2012. Before that club chapter, he had won the 1998 World Cup with France. The comeback and the World Cup belong to separate parts of his career.

lessons.title: Thierry Henry · Arsenal record
lessons.subtitle: Whole-club totals alongside Premier League-only numbers

story.title: His complete Arsenal record
story.body: Across his two Arsenal spells, Henry finished with 377 appearances and 228 goals in all competitions. These are whole-club totals, including the 2012 return, rather than Premier League-only counts.

story.title: The league-only view
story.body: The Premier League records 258 Arsenal appearances and 175 goals for Henry. The Premier League totals cover league matches only; the larger 377 appearance and 228 goal totals cover all competitions across his Arsenal career.

lessons.title: Dennis Bergkamp · career connections
lessons.subtitle: From Inter to an 11-year Arsenal chapter

story.title: Arriving from Italy
story.body: Bergkamp joined Arsenal from Inter Milan in 1995. He was a Dutch forward, and his arrival helped usher in a more technical style at Highbury.

story.title: A long stay at Arsenal
story.body: Bergkamp remained with Arsenal until the end of the 2005/06 campaign, when he retired. His final season closed an 11-year club chapter that began with his move from Inter.

lessons.title: Dennis Bergkamp · Arsenal record
lessons.subtitle: All-competition totals and Premier League-only output

story.title: The full Arsenal totals
story.body: Arsenal credits Bergkamp with 423 appearances and 120 goals across his complete club career. Those are all-competition Arsenal totals, not a count of Premier League matches alone.

story.title: Premier League numbers
story.body: In the Premier League, Bergkamp made 315 appearances and scored 87 goals. The league-only total is a subset of the broader Arsenal record; keeping the competition label attached prevents the counts from being confused.

lessons.title: From Dial Square to Arsenal
lessons.subtitle: Woolwich beginnings and a north London home

story.title: An industrial beginning
story.body: Arsenal began in 1886 with workers from the Woolwich Armaments factory, forming a football community in south-east London.

story.title: A move that reshaped the club
story.body: After financial trouble and relegation, the club moved to Highbury in 1913. Its first match there was a 2–1 win over Leicester Fosse.

lessons.title: The first Double
lessons.subtitle: A league title followed by an FA Cup final

story.title: A title in enemy territory
story.body: Arsenal clinched the 1970/71 league title at White Hart Lane, beating Tottenham 1–0 through Ray Kennedy.

story.title: A second trophy five days later
story.body: The club completed its first league-and-FA Cup Double by beating Liverpool 2–1 at Wembley.

lessons.title: Anfield, 26 May 1989
lessons.subtitle: A late goal decided the title on the final night

story.title: The final-day equation
story.body: Arsenal needed a two-goal win at Liverpool to take the league title. Alan Smith scored after a free kick, then Michael Thomas broke through in injury time.

story.title: A last-second finish
story.body: The 2–0 result delivered the championship to Arsenal at Anfield, a defining away victory in the club’s history.

lessons.title: Henry’s Highbury hat-trick
lessons.subtitle: A response that restored Arsenal’s momentum

story.title: A difficult week
story.body: After cup defeats ended Arsenal’s treble hopes, Liverpool led 2–1 at Highbury in April 2004.

story.title: Henry turns the match
story.body: Henry scored three times as Arsenal won 4–2, including a solo goal after running from inside the Liverpool half.

lessons.title: Henry’s 30-goal season
lessons.subtitle: A scoring award across three straight campaigns

story.title: A landmark league season
story.body: Henry scored 30 Premier League goals in Arsenal’s unbeaten 2003/04 title season.

story.title: A sustained run
story.body: He won the Golden Boot in three consecutive seasons from 2003/04 through 2005/06, and four times in total.

lessons.title: Bergkamp’s Newcastle finish
lessons.subtitle: A turn and finish chosen as a personal favourite

story.title: A goal remembered
story.body: Bergkamp selected his goal at Newcastle on 2 March 2002 among his favourite Arsenal goals.

story.title: Skill in a tight space
story.body: He described the finish as instinctive: he decided to go around the defender as the ball arrived, then scored.

lessons.title: The Leicester hat-trick
lessons.subtitle: A third goal became Bergkamp’s favourite

story.title: A night in 1997
story.body: Bergkamp’s favourite Arsenal goal came in the third goal of his hat-trick against Leicester City on 27 August 1997.

story.title: A brilliant finish, a shared result
story.body: He recalled controlling the ball, flicking it around a defender and finishing. Arsenal drew the match.

lessons.title: Shankly’s rebuild
lessons.subtitle: Promotion and a first league crown

story.title: A team rebuilt
story.body: Bill Shankly transformed Liverpool after taking charge in 1959. The club won promotion from the Second Division in 1962.

story.title: A new level of success
story.body: Liverpool became league champions in 1964, then won the club’s first FA Cup in 1965.

lessons.title: A long-awaited FA Cup
lessons.subtitle: Shankly’s Liverpool beat Leeds at Wembley

story.title: A first final win
story.body: Liverpool had reached earlier finals without lifting the Cup. On 1 May 1965, the team finally won it, defeating Leeds United 2–1 after extra time.

story.title: The decisive header
story.body: Ian St John scored the winner in the 111th minute.

lessons.title: Rome, 1984
lessons.subtitle: Liverpool won the European Cup on penalties at Roma’s home

story.title: A final at the opponent’s stadium
story.body: Liverpool met Roma at the Stadio Olimpico on 30 May 1984. The match finished 1–1 after extra time.

story.title: Penalties decide the trophy
story.body: Liverpool won the shoot-out 4–2. Ian Rush converted his penalty during the shoot-out, helping secure the club’s fourth European Cup.

lessons.title: Gerrard’s Cup final
lessons.subtitle: A late equaliser kept Liverpool in the 2006 final

story.title: West Ham lead twice
story.body: Liverpool trailed West Ham 2–0 and later 3–2 in the 2006 FA Cup final at Cardiff’s Millennium Stadium.

story.title: A goal from distance
story.body: Gerrard scored from around 30 yards in added time to make it 3–3. Liverpool won the shoot-out and the trophy.

lessons.title: The 2001 cup treble
lessons.subtitle: Three cup competitions, including the UEFA Cup final

story.title: A remarkable season
story.body: Liverpool won the League Cup, FA Cup and UEFA Cup in 2001. Gerrard started all three finals.

story.title: A European final goal
story.body: He scored in the 5–4 UEFA Cup final win over Alavés, a match decided by a golden goal.

lessons.title: Rush in the Rome shoot-out
lessons.subtitle: A personal career peak in the 1984 European Cup final

story.title: The first season treble
story.body: Rush’s 1983/84 campaign ended with Liverpool winning the league, League Cup and European Cup.

story.title: A daunting kick
story.body: In Rome, Rush converted his penalty in the shoot-out against Roma. He later called that kick the pinnacle of his career.

lessons.title: Rush’s 1983/84 scoring season
lessons.subtitle: A personal best across a trophy-winning campaign

story.title: An exceptional total
story.body: Rush scored 47 goals in all competitions for Liverpool in 1983/84, his personal best season with the club.

story.title: A season of silverware
story.body: He appeared 65 times as Liverpool won the league championship, League Cup and European Cup.

lessons.title: A club formed in Barcelona
lessons.subtitle: Gamper’s invitation grew into a football club

story.title: An open invitation
story.body: In October 1899, Joan Gamper placed an announcement inviting people interested in football to help form a club.

story.title: The founding meeting
story.body: On 29 November 1899, Gamper and eleven other men met in Barcelona and founded Foot-ball Club Barcelona.

lessons.title: Les Corts: Barça’s first great home
lessons.subtitle: The opening of a landmark stadium marked a new stage of growth

story.title: A growing club needed room
story.body: In the 1920s, Barcelona’s growing support prompted the construction of Les Corts, the club’s first great stadium.

story.title: A landmark opening
story.body: Les Corts opened on 20 May 1922 with an initial capacity of 22,000. Later enlargements tripled that capacity to 60,000, making the ground a visible marker of the club’s growth.

lessons.title: Wembley, 1992
lessons.subtitle: Koeman’s free kick delivered Barça’s first European Cup

story.title: A final reaches extra time
story.body: Barcelona and Sampdoria were goalless after 90 minutes in the European Cup final at Wembley.

story.title: A historic breakthrough
story.body: Ronald Koeman scored in the 111th minute for a 1–0 win, giving Barcelona its first European Cup.

lessons.title: Messi’s 91-goal year
lessons.subtitle: A calendar-year record split between club and country

story.title: A world record
story.body: Messi scored 91 goals in calendar year 2012, surpassing Gerd Müller’s previous mark of 85.

story.title: Two teams, one calendar year
story.body: The total comprised 79 goals for Barcelona and 12 for Argentina; keep the Barça portion separate from the overall record.

lessons.title: Five against Leverkusen
lessons.subtitle: Messi set a Champions League single-match scoring mark

story.title: A knockout-round rout
story.body: Barcelona beat Bayer Leverkusen 7–1 in the Champions League round of 16 second leg on 7 March 2012.

story.title: Five goals by one player
story.body: Messi scored five times, becoming the first player to score five goals in a single Champions League match.

lessons.title: Xavi’s international era
lessons.subtitle: Three consecutive major titles with Spain

story.title: European champions
story.body: Xavi was part of Spain’s European Championship-winning teams in 2008 and 2012.

story.title: World champion between them
story.body: Spain won the 2010 World Cup between those European titles, giving Xavi three successive major international tournament victories.

lessons.title: Xavi’s first-team debut
lessons.subtitle: A first appearance and first goal arrived together

story.title: From La Masia to the first team
story.body: After progressing through Barcelona’s youth teams, Xavi debuted for the first team in August 1998 against Mallorca.

story.title: An instant contribution
story.body: He scored in that Spanish Super Cup debut, beginning a 17-season first-team chapter at Barça.

lessons.title: Bayern · building a European powerhouse
lessons.subtitle: Bayern’s club timeline moves from its early success into the modern European era. The 1970s bec

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: Bayern’s club timeline moves from its early success into the modern European era. The 1970s became a defining period as domestic titles and European Cups brought a Munich side onto the continent’s biggest stage.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: The club’s milestones point to 1974, 1975 and 1976 as a three-year European Cup run. Those wins made the team of Beckenbauer, Maier and Müller a lasting reference point.

lessons.title: Bayern · the 2013 treble
lessons.subtitle: Jupp Heynckes’s Bayern turned the 2012/13 season into the club’s first treble: Bundesliga, DFB

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: Jupp Heynckes’s Bayern turned the 2012/13 season into the club’s first treble: Bundesliga, DFB Cup and Champions League. A strong league campaign had its title wrapped up early.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: The European final at Wembley against Borussia Dortmund supplied the season’s defining night. Arjen Robben scored the late winner, sealing the Champions League and completing the set.

lessons.title: Bayern · five goals in nine minutes
lessons.subtitle: On 22 September 2015, Bayern trailed Wolfsburg at half-time. Robert Lewandowski entered from th

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: On 22 September 2015, Bayern trailed Wolfsburg at half-time. Robert Lewandowski entered from the bench and changed the match in a burst that became one of the Bundesliga’s most famous scoring feats.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: His goals came in minutes 51, 52, 54, 57 and 60. The five-goal spell turned a 0–1 deficit into a 5–1 Bayern win.

lessons.title: Philipp Lahm · leadership and beginnings
lessons.subtitle: Lahm became Bayern captain in 2011 and led the club through its 2013 Champions League victory.

story.title: A steady captain
story.body: Lahm became Bayern captain in 2011 and led the club through its 2013 Champions League victory.

story.title: From youth football
story.body: He joined Bayern from FT Gern at age eleven and spent over two decades connected with the club, including a loan at Stuttgart.

lessons.title: Bastian Schweinsteiger · final setbacks and return
lessons.subtitle: The 2012 Champions League final at Bayern’s home ground ended with a penalty miss for Schweinst

story.title: A painful final
story.body: The 2012 Champions League final at Bayern’s home ground ended with a penalty miss for Schweinsteiger. He faced the setback again a year later at Wembley.

story.title: Back at the summit
story.body: Bayern’s 2013 Champions League win completed his return from the previous final. In 2015, after 17 years at the club, he left for Manchester United.

lessons.title: Dortmund · the Hitzfeld ascent
lessons.subtitle: Ottmar Hitzfeld’s Dortmund rose through the Bundesliga in the 1990s. The club won consecutive l

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: Ottmar Hitzfeld’s Dortmund rose through the Bundesliga in the 1990s. The club won consecutive league titles before reaching the summit of Europe in 1997.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: The Champions League final paired Dortmund with defending champions Juventus in Munich. Dortmund won 3–1, becoming the first German club to win the competition in its then-current Champions League format.

lessons.title: Dortmund · a record-setting double
lessons.subtitle: Dortmund defended the Bundesliga title in 2012 and then won the DFB Pokal final against Bayern.

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: Dortmund defended the Bundesliga title in 2012 and then won the DFB Pokal final against Bayern. It was the club’s first domestic double.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: The league campaign closed with 81 points, then a Bundesliga record. In Berlin, Robert Lewandowski scored a hat-trick as Dortmund beat Bayern 5–2.

lessons.title: Dortmund · Wembley’s all-German final
lessons.subtitle: Dortmund’s 2012/13 European run carried Jürgen Klopp’s side to Wembley. A 4–1 first-leg win ove

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: Dortmund’s 2012/13 European run carried Jürgen Klopp’s side to Wembley. A 4–1 first-leg win over Real Madrid in the semi-final put them within reach of the Champions League final.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: The final became the first all-German pairing in the competition. Bayern won 2–1 with a late Arjen Robben goal, leaving Dortmund as runners-up.

story.body: Reus won his first major title with Dortmund in the 2017 DFB-Pokal final against Eintracht Frankfurt.

story.title: Success and setback
story.body: He suffered a cruciate ligament tear in that same final. BVB’s 2018 contract announcement looks back on the trophy and the recovery together.

lessons.subtitle: Leverkusen’s first major trophy came in the 1988 UEFA Cup. Espanyol won the first leg 3–0, leav

story.title: Set the scene
story.body: Leverkusen’s first major trophy came in the 1988 UEFA Cup. Espanyol won the first leg 3–0, leaving the German side with a daunting task at home.

story.title: Remember the detail
story.body: At the Ulrich Haberland Stadium on 18 May, Leverkusen matched the aggregate score and then won the shootout. The comeback became known as the Miracle of Leverkusen.

lessons.title: Leverkusen · first German championship
lessons.subtitle: Bayer 04’s first Bundesliga championship arrived in 2024, ending Bayern Munich’s run of 11 cons

story.title: The title-clinching day
story.body: On 14 April 2024, Leverkusen beat Werder Bremen 5–0 to clinch its first Bundesliga title.

story.title: Finish the league unbeaten
story.body: The final matchday win against Augsburg completed the unbeaten league campaign. Keep that season-ending match separate from the earlier title-clinching win over Bremen.

lessons.title: Leverkusen · the cup final seals the double
lessons.subtitle: Xhaka’s strike secured the second half of the domestic double.

story.title: One goal in Berlin
story.body: Leverkusen beat Kaiserslautern 1–0 in the 2023/24 DFB-Pokal final. Granit Xhaka scored the winner after 16 minutes.

story.title: A second cup
story.body: This was Leverkusen’s second DFB-Pokal title. Paired with its first Bundesliga championship, the win completed the domestic double.

lessons.title: Philipp Lahm · longevity and honours
lessons.subtitle: The lasting scale of a two-decade Bayern career

story.title: A long Bayern chapter
story.body: Lahm spent more than twenty years connected to Bayern, beginning in the youth ranks and ending his playing career at 33.

story.title: A collection of titles
story.body: Across 22 years with the club, he won 21 honours. The count shows the scale of the era he helped lead.

lessons.title: Bastian Schweinsteiger · from youth to first team
lessons.subtitle: A teenage academy arrival grew into the Bayern senior side

story.title: Youth move
story.body: At 13, Schweinsteiger moved from TSV 1860 Rosenheim to Bayern’s Säbener Straße academy. He collected titles with both the U17 and U19 teams.

story.title: First-team step
story.body: The midfielder made his first-team debut at 18. His path from academy player to a central figure in the senior team started early.

lessons.title: A comeback sends Xolos to the 2012 final
lessons.subtitle: Tijuana overturned a two-goal first-leg deficit against León in a charged semifinal return.

story.title: Back from León
story.body: After losing the first leg 2–0, Xolos returned to Estadio Caliente needing a response in the Apertura 2012 semifinal.

story.title: The turn
story.body: A 3–0 home win reversed the tie 3–2 on aggregate and sent Club Tijuana into its first top-flight final.

lessons.title: Riascos rescues a point against Atlas
lessons.subtitle: A September 2012 equalizer kept Xolos unbeaten at home through five Apertura matches.

story.title: A difficult afternoon
story.body: Atlas took the lead at Estadio Caliente, but Riascos kept attacking and drew Xolos level late in the match.

story.title: A home draw
story.body: His 75th-minute finish made it 1–1 on September 22, 2012, in Apertura matchday nine.

lessons.title: A dated scoring mark in Morelia
lessons.subtitle: Riascos reached two personal Xolos milestones during a 1–1 draw on October 27, 2012.

story.title: A goal in the ninth minute
story.body: Riascos opened the scoring at Morelia on October 27, 2012, with his seventh league goal of that season.

story.title: A club scoring mark
story.body: That goal brought him to 12 Xolos goals across his first two top-flight campaigns, level with José Sand as the club’s leading Primera División scorers at the time.

lessons.title: Saucedo’s Clausura 2012 goalkeeping record
lessons.subtitle: He was the least scored-on goalkeeper in the regular phase and received an award nomination.

story.title: A low-conceding campaign
story.body: In the Clausura 2012 regular phase, Saucedo appeared in all 17 matches and conceded 11 goals.

story.title: Across 19 appearances
story.body: Including the quarterfinals, he played 19 times and kept eight clean sheets. The federation named him among the candidates for the tournament’s goalkeeper award.

lessons.title: A first captain’s armband at match 66
lessons.subtitle: Saucedo led Xolos for the first time in a 2–0 home win during Clausura 2013.

story.title: A milestone match
story.body: Saucedo started in goal against Atlante in Clausura 2013, his 66th appearance for Club Tijuana.

story.title: First time as captain
story.body: He wore the Xolos captain’s armband for the first time as the team won 2–0 and recorded its third clean sheet of that campaign.

lessons.title: A free kick in Arce’s 401st league appearance
lessons.subtitle: Arce scored from distance in Xolos’s Apertura 2012 opening win over Puebla.

story.title: A milestone opener
story.body: On July 20, 2012, Xolos began Apertura with a 2–0 victory over Puebla. Arce opened the scoring from a free kick.

story.title: A landmark appearance
story.body: The goal came in Arce’s 401st Primera División match, making a league-career milestone part of the club’s first win of the tournament.

lessons.title: Arce scores in Xolos’s first top-flight win
lessons.subtitle: His goal helped deliver a 3–1 victory away to Santos in August 2011.

story.title: A first win
story.body: Xolos earned their first victory in Mexico’s top division on August 6, 2011, away to Santos Laguna.

story.title: Arce on the scoresheet
story.body: Arce scored in the 43rd minute as Club Tijuana rallied to a 3–1 result in Torreón.

lessons.title: Paris, 2000: La Octava
lessons.subtitle: Real Madrid win the first all-Spanish European Cup final

story.title: A final between Spanish rivals
story.body: Real Madrid and Valencia met in the European Cup final in Paris on 24 May 2000.

story.title: Three goals, a clean sheet
story.body: Fernando Morientes, Steve McManaman and Raúl scored in a 3–0 victory, giving Madrid its eighth European Cup.

lessons.title: Ronaldo’s two-goal Cardiff final
lessons.subtitle: Madrid defeat Juventus in 2017

story.title: A final in Wales
story.body: Real Madrid met Juventus in Cardiff on 3 June 2017.

story.title: Ronaldo decides it
story.body: Cristiano Ronaldo scored twice in a 4–1 win and was named man of the match.

lessons.title: Ronaldo’s Madrid scoring records
lessons.subtitle: Milestones across nine seasons

story.title: Goals in every competition
story.body: Real Madrid’s profile records Ronaldo’s goals across LaLiga, the Champions League, domestic cups and international club competitions.

story.title: An extraordinary peak
story.body: The club also records 61 goals in a single season and six Champions League top-scorer awards during his Madrid years.

lessons.title: Ramos scores in another world final
lessons.subtitle: Real Madrid beat Al Ain in 2018

story.title: The final in Abu Dhabi
story.body: Real Madrid faced Al Ain in the 2018 FIFA Club World Cup final.

story.title: A captain’s header
story.body: Ramos scored Madrid’s third goal as the team won 4–1 and claimed its fourth Club World Cup.

lessons.title: Ramos’s individual honours
lessons.subtitle: Recognition across a long career

story.title: Repeated World XI selection
story.body: Ramos was selected for the FIFA FIFPro World 11 eleven times.

story.title: Defensive distinction
story.body: He was named the Champions League’s best defender in both 2017 and 2018, and earned the Club World Cup Golden Ball in 2014.

lessons.title: Casillas takes over in Glasgow
lessons.subtitle: A decisive substitute appearance in the 2002 final

story.title: An injury changes the final
story.body: Real Madrid met Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League final at Hampden Park on 15 May 2002.

story.title: Casillas enters the match
story.body: After César was injured, Casillas came on and made key saves as Madrid protected its 2–1 lead.

lessons.title: Casillas’s goalkeeper honours
lessons.subtitle: International and individual recognition

story.title: A decorated international
story.body: Casillas won the World Cup and two European Championships with Spain.

story.title: A global goalkeeper award
story.body: He was selected for the FIFA FIFPro World XI five times and named the world’s best goalkeeper by IFFHS five times.

lessons.title: Raúl’s double at Old Trafford
lessons.subtitle: Redondo sets up a quarter-final classic

story.title: A difficult away tie
story.body: Madrid visited Manchester United in the Champions League quarter-final on 19 April 2000 after a goalless first leg.

story.title: Two goals settle it
story.body: Raúl scored twice in a 3–2 win at Old Trafford, helping Madrid advance toward the eighth European Cup.

lessons.title: Raúl’s long Madrid era
lessons.subtitle: Sixteen seasons and six league titles

story.title: A first-team mainstay
story.body: Raúl represented Real Madrid for 16 seasons, from his promotion to the first team in 1994 until 2010.

story.title: Domestic success
story.body: Among his honours were six LaLiga titles and two Intercontinental Cups.

lessons.title: Benzema helps finish the City comeback
lessons.subtitle: A penalty sends Madrid into the final

story.title: Madrid trail late
story.body: In the Champions League semi-final second leg on 4 May 2022, Madrid were behind Manchester City 1–0 in the 89th minute.

story.title: Extra time decides the tie
story.body: After Rodrygo’s two late goals forced extra time, Benzema converted a penalty to send Madrid through.

lessons.title: Benzema scores in a Nations League final
lessons.subtitle: France defeat Spain in 2021

story.title: A final in Milan
story.body: France faced Spain in the UEFA Nations League final on 10 October 2021.

story.title: A quick response
story.body: After Spain scored first, Benzema equalised for France before Kylian Mbappé scored the winner.

lessons.title: Zidane’s late Madrid-season brace
lessons.subtitle: A 4–0 win over Espanyol

story.title: A final Madrid campaign
story.body: In 2005/06, Zidane delivered one of his last standout performances for Madrid against Espanyol.

story.title: Two goals in a rout
story.body: Madrid won 4–0 at the Bernabéu, with Zidane scoring twice, including the goal that sealed the result.

lessons.title: Zidane’s three straight European Cups as coach
lessons.subtitle: A rare run from 2016 to 2018

story.title: A new role
story.body: After his playing career, Zidane returned to lead Real Madrid from the dugout.

story.title: Three in succession
story.body: He guided the club to Champions League titles in 2016, 2017 and 2018, becoming the first coach to win three successive editions.

lessons.title: Bale’s Club World Cup semi-final hat-trick
lessons.subtitle: Madrid beat Kashima Antlers

story.title: A place in the final
story.body: Madrid faced Kashima Antlers in the 2018 Club World Cup semi-final in Abu Dhabi.

story.title: Bale takes control
story.body: Bale scored a hat-trick, sending Madrid through to the final and earning the tournament’s Golden Ball.

lessons.title: Bale’s Madrid honours
lessons.subtitle: Nine years and 19 trophies

story.title: A long spell in Madrid
story.body: Bale spent nine years with Real Madrid after arriving in 2013.

story.title: A decorated era
story.body: The club credits him with 19 trophies and names him the best player of the 2018 Champions League final.

lessons.title: Roberto Carlos scores in Monaco
lessons.subtitle: Madrid beat Feyenoord in 2002

story.title: Madrid return to Europe
story.body: After winning La Novena, Real Madrid met Feyenoord in the 2002 European Super Cup.

story.title: A goal from the left-back
story.body: Roberto Carlos scored in a 3–1 win at the Stade Louis II in Monaco.

lessons.title: Roberto Carlos with Brazil
lessons.subtitle: A world champion in 2002

story.title: A famous national team
story.body: Roberto Carlos represented Brazil, winning the 2002 FIFA World Cup.

story.title: A role in the final

story.body: A group of Turin schoolboys created Juventus in 1897. Its first home ground was Piazza d’Armi, and its first shirts were pink.

lessons.title: Napoli’s layered beginnings

lessons.title: Napoli win their first Scudetto
lessons.subtitle: A 2–1 win over Milan in 1987

story.title: A defining league night
story.body: Napoli beat Milan 2–1 on 26 April 1987, moving toward the first league title in the club’s history.

story.title: Maradona and Carnevale
story.body: Andrea Carnevale opened the scoring before Diego Maradona added Napoli’s second goal. The title was confirmed two weeks later.

lessons.title: Napoli clinch a third Scudetto
lessons.subtitle: A draw at Udinese ends the wait

story.title: The title is secured
story.body: Napoli drew 1–1 away to Udinese in May 2023, securing the club’s third Italian championship.

story.title: Osimhen makes the difference
story.body: Victor Osimhen scored Napoli’s equaliser in the second half, setting off celebrations among the travelling supporters.

lessons.title: Maradona’s Napoli chapter
lessons.subtitle: From Barcelona to southern Italy

story.title: A major signing
story.body: Diego Maradona joined Napoli in 1984 after playing for Barcelona.

story.title: A lasting influence
story.body: His time at the club included two Serie A titles and the 1989 UEFA Cup, achievements that reshaped Napoli’s standing in Italian and European football.

lessons.title: Maradona leads Napoli to the UEFA Cup
lessons.subtitle: The 1989 final against Stuttgart

story.body: Napoli faced Stuttgart in the 1989 UEFA Cup final. Maradona scored from the penalty spot in the first leg.

story.title: A European breakthrough

lessons.title: Maradona’s Napoli honours
lessons.subtitle: Two league titles and a European Cup

story.title: A historic run
story.body: Maradona’s Napoli years brought the club its first Scudetto in 1987 and a second in 1990.

story.title: Europe follows
story.body: Napoli also won the 1989 UEFA Cup during his spell, completing a rare run of domestic and continental success.

lessons.title: Maradona’s 1986 World Cup
lessons.subtitle: Captain of champions

story.title: Argentina lift the trophy
story.body: Maradona captained Argentina to the 1986 FIFA World Cup title in Mexico.

story.title: A leading contribution
story.body: He scored five goals and provided four assists during the tournament, helping Argentina become world champions.

story.title: Two stages in Italy

story.body: Napoli met Juventus in the Coppa Italia final on 20 May 2012.

story.body: Hamšík scored as Napoli beat Juventus 2–0, lifting the club’s first trophy since 1990.

lessons.title: From Récord to América
lessons.subtitle: A schoolyard team became a four-time champion.

story.title: A team takes shape
story.body: Students Rafael Garza Gutiérrez and Germán Núñez Cortina brought together classmates in 1916. The team took its name at a meeting in the Condesa neighborhood on October 12.

story.title: A run of titles
story.body: After returning to the name América in 1920, the club won four consecutive league championships from 1924–25 through 1927–28.

lessons.title: The first star arrives
lessons.subtitle: An unbeaten season ended with a late winner.

story.title: A perfect finish
story.body: América’s first championship came in the amateur-era 1924–25 season. The team clinched it with a narrow win over Asturias in March 1925.

story.title: A measured campaign
story.body: The club’s account records ten wins and two draws across twelve matches, with just four goals conceded.

lessons.title: Three titles in the 1980s
lessons.subtitle: A rivalry final opened a championship streak.

story.title: A final against Guadalajara
story.body: América beat Guadalajara in the 1983–84 final to earn its eighth championship. The club describes that victory as the start of a three-title run.

story.title: Three consecutive crowns
story.body: The next two league championships followed in 1984–85 and Prode 1985, turning the initial final win into a historic sequence.

lessons.title: A Guadalajara club
lessons.subtitle: The 1906 side grew into the Campeonísimo.

story.title: A long-running club
story.body: Club Deportivo Guadalajara dates its foundation to May 8, 1906. The team that became known as Chivas later defined a celebrated stretch of Mexican football.

story.title: The Campeonísimo era
story.body: From 1957 to 1970, the club’s account credits this generation with a broad collection of domestic and international honors.

lessons.title: The 2017 double
lessons.subtitle: Chivas paired a league crown with the Copa MX.

story.title: A short-tournament first
story.body: Chivas says its Clausura 2017 achievement made it the first club to complete the League-and-Cup double in the short-tournament era.

story.title: A league final at home
story.body: The team sealed the league title against Tigres at Estadio Akron, with goals from Alan Pulido and José Juan Vázquez.

lessons.title: Chivas on the South American stage
lessons.subtitle: A historic run reached the 2010 Libertadores final.

story.title: An international campaign
story.body: Chivas reached its first Copa Libertadores final in 2010 after eliminating Universidad de Chile in the semifinal.

story.title: A narrow defeat
story.body: The final against Internacional began with Chivas in front, but the Brazilian club came back to win the trophy.

lessons.title: From Toluca to the top flight
lessons.subtitle: The Diablos turned a city club into a national power.

story.title: A 1917 beginning
story.body: Deportivo Toluca FC was founded on February 12, 1917. Its early history moved through amateur football before the club entered the professional pyramid.

story.title: Promotion and progress
story.body: The club joined the Second Division in 1950 and won promotion to the First Division in January 1953.

lessons.title: Back-to-back champions
lessons.subtitle: Ignacio Trelles guided Toluca’s first two league crowns.

story.title: A first championship
story.body: Toluca won its first league title in 1967 with Ignacio Trelles as coach and Amaury Epaminondas leading the tournament’s scoring.

story.title: A title defended
story.body: The Diablos followed that success by retaining the championship in 1968, securing their first consecutive league crowns.

lessons.title: Two finals, decided from the spot
lessons.subtitle: Penalties delivered Toluca’s fifth and ninth stars.

story.title: A dramatic win over Atlas
story.body: The 1999 final with Atlas finished level over two legs and extra time. Toluca prevailed in the sudden-death shootout when Hernán Cristante saved the decisive attempt.

story.title: Another shootout triumph
story.body: In 2008, Toluca again needed penalties after Cruz Azul drew level on aggregate. Cristante stopped Alejandro Vela’s kick to clinch another title.

lessons.title: A mark among América’s scorers
lessons.subtitle: A goal against Santos put Henry Martín on a historic list.

story.title: A milestone in 2022
story.body: Against Santos Laguna on September 15, 2022, Martín scored his 64th goal for América, tying Antonio Carlos Santos.

story.title: A season in motion
story.body: The club said the goal was his ninth of that season; it also placed him 13th among América’s historic scorers at that point.

lessons.title: A brace in Puebla
lessons.subtitle: Martín scored twice as América built a 6–1 first-leg lead in the 2022 quarterfinal.

story.title: A brace away from home
story.body: Martín struck in the 33rd minute of América’s 2022 quarterfinal first leg in Puebla.

story.title: A commanding result
story.body: He added a second goal after halftime, helping América win 6–1.

lessons.title: From Mérida to the first team
lessons.subtitle: Henry Martín moved from amateur football in Yucatán into the professional game and made his Liga MX debut with Tijuana.

story.title: Starting in Mérida
story.body: Martín began his professional path in Mérida in 2013, then joined Tijuana for the Apertura 2014.

story.title: A first-team start
story.body: He entered Liga MX against América and started the match; his early season also brought his first league goal.

story.title: A derby penalty
story.body: Martín converted a penalty against Guadalajara in the Apertura 2022 Clásico at Estadio Azteca.

story.title: A double-digit season

lessons.title: His first league championship

story.title: An unbeaten run
story.body: The same account notes a 30-match unbeaten streak associated with that first championship period.

lessons.title: Guillermo Ochoa · Captain at Tokyo 2020

story.body: In the 3–0 group-stage win over South Africa, Ochoa started for Mexico and then gathered his teammates as captain.

story.title: A captain’s message
story.body: After the win, Ochoa gathered the team and told them they were one match from playing for medals. The lesson connects his starting role with his leadership in that tournament.

story.title: Six editions
story.body: FIFA’s retrospective describes Ochoa’s sixth World Cup as the endpoint of a long international career.

story.title: A rare Mexican record
story.body: FIFA notes that no Mexican had previously reached six consecutive World Cups as a player.

lessons.title: A debut with a goal
lessons.subtitle: Hernández’s first senior minutes for Chivas came against Necaxa.

story.title: September 2006
story.body: At Estadio Jalisco, José Manuel de la Torre brought Hernández on against Necaxa.

story.title: Immediate impact
story.body: Hernández scored before the match ended and joined the championship-winning squad that semester.

lessons.title: A scoring crown in 2010
lessons.subtitle: Hernández won the Bicentenario 2010 scoring title in limited appearances.

story.title: Top scorer
story.body: Chivas records him as the tournament’s individual scoring champion with ten goals.

story.title: Efficiency
story.body: He achieved the honor despite playing six fewer games than the other forwards cited by the club.

lessons.title: The first goal at Estadio Omnilife

story.title: A varied record
story.body: The club’s breakdown includes league, continental, and domestic cup competitions.

lessons.subtitle: Salcido’s first senior appearance for Chivas came in July 2001.

lessons.title: Captain of the 2017 double

story.body: Chivas identifies Salcido as captain and a key player in the Clausura 2017 double.

story.title: Two domestic trophies

story.title: A long service record

story.title: Before and after Toluca
story.body: The cited career timeline places Olimpia before Cardozo’s 1995–2005 Toluca spell, and San Lorenzo after it. Keep these playing clubs separate from his later coaching jobs.

lessons.title: Cardozo’s scoring records

story.title: Decisive in 1999

story.title: Decisive again in 2008

lessons.title: A rebound and a final save in 2008

story.title: A shootout swing
story.body: During the Apertura 2008 shootout, a shot struck Cruz Azul goalkeeper Yosgart Gutiérrez and rebounded into the net, prolonging the series.

story.title: The final stop
story.body: Cristante then saved Alejandro Vela’s penalty, and Toluca celebrated its ninth league title.
